outcome: Classification of narrow pelvises (normal, suspected narrowness, narrow pelvis)
cohort: The study selected 214 women aged 15 to 55 years, comprising 171 who had vaginal deliveries and 43 who underwent caesarean sections due to feto-pelvic disproportion of maternal origin.
finding: The Anterior Pelvic Index (API) is a good tool for predicting women with suspected narrow pelvis and allows for its classification into three types: suitable for vaginal delivery, suspected pelvic narrowness, and confirmed narrow pelvis, with specific cut-off points.
mod_finding: An API value > 15.83 indicates a pelvis suitable for vaginal delivery; values between 14.19 and 15.83 suggest suspected pelvic narrowness; and values < 14.19 confirm a narrow pelvis, directly correlating with the likelihood of vaginal delivery versus caesarean section due to FPD.
cross-section timing: The API was calculated in women who had already experienced either vaginal delivery or caesarean section due to FPD, suggesting the data collection for API and delivery outcome was cross-sectional around the time of birth events.
